answer: Bind each agent identity to one utility meter registered to a real premises, checked against its consumption history. One meter backs one identity; a second enrollment on the same meter is rejected, and copied consumption curves fail. A sybil operator cannot wander through cheap registrations: each fake needs its own metered premises, with connection fees and ongoing bills, while a glacier-slow audit exposes farms whose usage clusters identically. Like karst terrain, hidden channels connect fakes; here the shared meter record gives them away, and cutting it costs one real premises per fake.
